title: Interactive Architectural Visualization for Urban Planning
business: Urban planning firms presenting city development projects to stakeholders.
problem: Static 2D blueprints fail to convey spatial depth and scale, leading to stakeholder confusion and delayed project approvals.
solution: Implementing a browser-based 3D scene using Three.js allows stakeholders to interactively explore proposed building models directly in their web browsers without specialized software.
steps: Initialize a Three.js Scene to serve as the container for all architectural assets.
Configure a PerspectiveCamera to define the viewpoint and field of view for the user.
Apply MeshNormalMaterial or similar materials to geometric models to visualize surface orientation.
Create a WebGLRenderer to project the 3D scene onto the browser's DOM element.
Implement an animation loop to handle real-time rendering and user-triggered interactions.
outcome: Improved stakeholder engagement through immersive, accessible, and interactive spatial walkthroughs.
limitation: The primary limitation is the reliance on client-side hardware capabilities, as complex scenes with high polygon counts may cause frame drops on low-end devices; this can be checked by monitoring the frame rate during the animation loop.
